Indian Standard 

METHODS OF SAMPLING AND 

TEST ( PHYSICAL AND CHEMICAL) FOR 

WATER AND WASTEWATER 

PART 30 BROMIDE 

( First Revision ) 



1. Scope —This standard prescribes two methods for determination of bromide. Bromides in 
the samples are oxidized to bromine in presence of phenol red and subsequently phenol red is 
brominated by addition of chloramine-T. The brominated compound thus produced is reddish 
to violet depending upon its concentration. The concentration of chioramine-T and the timing 
of reaction before dechlorination are critical. The colour maching is done either visually or using 
a spectrophotometer. In case of any difference of opinion, the spectrophotometric method shall 
be the referee method. 

2. Interference — Ions commonly found in water do not interfere in the test, but oxidizing and 
reducing agents and iodides do interfere. 

3. Apparatus 

3.1 Spectrophotometer — for use at 590 nm, providing a light path of at least 2 cm. 

3.2 Nessler Cyclinders — 100 ml capacity. 

4. Reagents 

4.1 Acetate Buffer Solution — D\sso\ye 68 g sodium acetate trihydrate ( NaC2H302.3H20 ) in 
distilled water. Add 30 ml of glacial acetic acid and make up to 1 litre. The pH should be 4*6 to 
4-7. 

4.2 Piienol Red Iridicator Solution — Dissolve 0*021 g phenol red ( phenol sulphonaphthalein 
sodium salt ) and dilute to 1 00 ml with distilled water. 

4.3 C/?/ora/77/A7e-rSo/wf/b/? — Dissolve 0-5 g chloramine-T and dilute to 100 ml with distilled 
water. Store in a dark bottle in refrigerator. 

4.4 Sodium Thiosulphate Solution — 2 N. Dissolve 496 g of sodium thiosulphate ( Na2S203,5H20 or 
31-6 g Na2S203 ) and dilute to 100 ml with distilled water. 

4.5 Stock Bromide Solution — Dissolve 744"6 mg anhydrous potassium bromide ( KBr ) in 
distilled water and make up to 1 litre. One milliiitre of the solution == 50 mg Br. 

4o.1 Standard bromide solution — Dilute 10*0 ml of stock solution to 1 litre. One milliiitre of 
the diltuted solution = 5 00 /tg Br. 

5. F*rocedure — Take 50 ml or an aliquot of sample diluted to 50 ml containing 1 to 1*0 mg/1 
of bromide. Add 2 ml buffer solution, 2 ml phenol red solution and 50 ml chloramine-T solution. 
Mix thoroughly and allow to stand for exactly 20 minutes. Dechlorinate by mixing with 0*5 ml 
of sodium thiosulphate solution. Compare colour visually in Nessler cylinders against bromide 
standards prepared simultaneously with the sample or preferably read absorbance \n a spectro- 
photometer at 590 nm against reagent blank. Determine mg of bromide per litre against 
absorbance from a calibration curve. 

6. Calculation

IS : 3025 ( Part 30 ) -1988 

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

Bromide may occur in varying amounts in well supplies in coastal areas as a result of sea 
water intrusion. Industrial discharges may contribute the bromide found in some fresh water 
streams. Under normal circumstances, the bromide content of most drinking waters is negligible, 
seldom exceeding 1 mg/l. This standard supersedes 26 of IS : 3025-1964 'Methods of sampling 
and test ( physical and chemical ) for water used in industry'.
